question: Which of the following is an example of a homeothermic animal?
solution:
The correct answer is **Penguin.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **homeothermic animal** is one that can maintain a relatively constant internal body temperature regardless of external temperature fluctuations. 
 
• **Penguins** are an example of homeothermic animals.
 
• Penguins are birds and, like most birds and mammals, are endothermic or warm-blooded. 
 
• Penguins can generate and regulate their body heat internally. Penguins have specialized adaptations to survive in cold environments, such as a layer of insulating feathers and a thick layer of blubber. Despite living in extremely cold conditions, penguins maintain a stable internal body temperature.
 
• Salamander: Salamanders are ectothermic animals. They cannot internally regulate their body temperature and rely on external sources, such as the environment, to control their body temperature.
 
• Cobra: Cobras are reptiles and, like other reptiles, are ectothermic. They need external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature and cannot maintain a constant internal temperature.
 
• Tortoise: Tortoises are also reptiles and ectothermic. They depend on the external environment for temperature regulation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Ectothermic Animals: These animals, including reptiles and amphibians, rely on external sources of heat to regulate their body temperature. 

 
 
• They are often referred to as cold-blooded, but this doesn't mean their blood is cold; rather, their internal temperature varies with the environment.
 
 
 
• Endothermic Animals: These animals, such as mammals and birds, can generate and regulate their body heat internally. 
 
 
• They are often referred to as warm-blooded because they can maintain a relatively constant internal temperature, independent of external conditions. 
 
• Homeothermic animals are a subset of endothermic animals that actively maintain a stable internal body temperature.
